scripts.typecheck: node scripts/queue-run.js --tsc -- sh -c 'tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.strict.json --noEmit && node scripts/typecheck-mods.js'
scripts.check:sh: sh scripts/lib/serialised.sh check:sh shellcheck shellcheck -x --severity=style --exclude=SC2016 $(node scripts/lib/formatters.js shell-files --tracked)

comments.scripts.typecheck: Five passes, deliberately. The first is the whole repo on tsconfig.json; the second re-checks app/ and lib/, and the programs under scripts/ and the skills' scripts/ minus their test files, under tsconfig.strict.json, whose only addition is noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Why tests are out, and the only shapes a finding may be cleared with: that file's own header (mantahostels#1064, #1336). tsc has no per-path compilerOptions, so a second config file is the only way to scope a flag. Every pass must stay in this one script: .husky/pre-commit and ci.yml each run `npm run typecheck` and neither knows about the other configs. The third and fourth type-check the delivery and liveness mods, which run in the engine's plugin environment rather than Node and so each have their own tsconfig.json and engine declarations (#854, #865). The fifth checks the plugin's entry module, which imports both, with both mods' state contracts, which the release composes into the one the plugin ships (#946, #3251). scripts/typecheck-mods.js runs those three, copying the untracked engine declarations in first and skipping, with a warning, where this machine has none (#1960).
comments.scripts.check:eslint: ESLint over app/ and lib/, the only surface eslint.config.mjs declares a `files` key for. --max-warnings 0 because several rules default to warn rather than error (@next/next/no-css-tags and react-hooks/exhaustive-deps among them) and eslint exits 0 on a warning. A rule that turns out noisy is downgraded in eslint.config.mjs rather than by softening this flag. Two callers, both hard-failing: ci.yml's Lint and tests job, and .husky/pre-commit, which passes the commit's own staged paths instead of running this script. Why ESLint is kept at all when Biome 2.5 already owns useHookAtTopLevel and useExhaustiveDependencies: the 20 @next/next framework rules have no Biome equivalent (mantahostels#1133).
comments.scripts.test:changed: vitest over the test files reachable from what git reports as changed, for mid-session iteration. SINCE mantahostels#3208 bare `npm run test` narrows the same way by default — against `merge-base(HEAD, origin/main)` rather than this script's working-tree-against-HEAD — escalating to the whole suite only where narrowing would be worthless (a stale or unreadable read-graph manifest, a `package.json` hunk outside mantahostels#2160's allow-list, or a diff that cannot be read). `npm run test -- --full=<cause>` (#182 requires the cause) is the whole suite; the push rule (docs/agents/rules/push-green-suite.txt) now asks for the BARE run (mantahostels#3210). THE DEFAULT'S NARROWED RUN IS ITSELF ADMISSIBLE at the push gate on the same terms as this script's — it synthesises an argv of nothing but --changed and its base — so what separates the two is now the BASE they diff against, not the certificate: this one reads the working tree against HEAD, the default reads merge-base(HEAD, origin/main), so on a clean tree this one selects nothing and the default still selects the branch's own commits. A SEPARATE NAME RATHER THAN A FLAG ON `test`, kept though mantahostels#3208 left the two certificates identical: what the name still buys is the BASE above, not a weaker marker. SINCE mantahostels#2146 a filtered run can still satisfy the push gate, as a SEPARATE weaker certificate: the wrapper checks docs/test-read-edges.json against the tree and, where it is fresh and argv carried nothing but --changed, marks the run admissible; a full certificate is still a full run's alone (mantahostels#1230). Takes the same git-ref argument vitest does (`npm run test:changed -- HEAD~3`). ROUTED THROUGH scripts/run-vitest.js SINCE mantahostels#2002, so it gets the stall watchdog and the log tee. SINCE mantahostels#2095 the wrapper CONSUMES --changed rather than forwarding it: it takes vitest's own import-graph selection, unions in the runtime readers docs/test-read-edges.json records for the same diff, and hands vitest that explicit file list — which is why the selection includes tests that read a changed document without importing it.
comments.scripts.check:sh: shellcheck over every tracked shell file, as scripts/lib/formatters.js's shellFiles() picks them (#1828): a husky hook, a .sh or .bash file, or an extensionless file whose shebang names a shell, minus what .gitattributes marks linguist-vendored or linguist-generated. Gated at --severity=style with one code excluded (#1315 Q2, #1331, #3032), so the info and style tiers refuse too. SC2016 (a $ in single quotes) flags the backticks and $ the house writes on purpose in message text and jq or node -e programs. Any other false finding carries an inline disable with its reason. SC2148 (no shebang) is not excluded: a sourced, shebang-less script opens with a `# shellcheck shell=` directive instead of being excluded by code (#753), so a script that is run and lost its shebang still fails. -x makes shellcheck follow sourced libs, which only works because each source line carries a `# shellcheck source=` directive — every guard sources through "$here/lib/...", a path shellcheck cannot resolve statically. Add that directive to a new source line rather than adding an -e exclusion. .agents/skills/ is out by .gitattributes: its .sh is a vendored skill template carrying placeholders, not runnable shell. If the lister fails, shellcheck is handed no file and exits 3, so the run fails rather than passing empty. A comment line BEGINNING `# shellcheck ` is parsed as a directive and SC1073-errors the whole file, so reflow prose that happens to open with the word. It runs under scripts/lib/serialised.sh's machine-wide shellcheck lock, shared with check:sh:changed and the pre-commit gate (#2627). Run scoped, per staged path, by .husky/pre-commit since mantahostels#1134: -x follows source= directives DOWNWARD from each path given, so scoping does not break it. DELIBERATELY ONE INVOCATION, not chunked across xargs workers: mantahostels#3544 shipped that form and measured it on the runner, where the step did not halve and no billed minute moved (n=1). Re-measure ON THE RUNNER before re-proposing — a local timing will not show it (mantahostels#313), and mantahostels#3544 carries the baseline to compare against. THE VERSION IS PINNED ON BOTH SIDES (#124): ci.yml's Shellcheck step fetches v0.11.0 by checksum rather than using the runner image's preinstalled 0.9.0, so this command and that step run the same binary. Local is the same version, hand-placed in ~/.local/bin (docs/agents/rules/shellcheck-not-installed.txt). Bump the two together or this command stops predicting CI. The pin is PROSPECTIVE: run over the same tree, the two versions agreed (#124).
comments.scripts.check:sh:format: shfmt at -i 2 -ci over the same file set as check:sh (#1332, ruled at #1315 Q3): it refuses layout alone, as Biome's formatter does for JS and TS. scripts/check-shfmt.js wraps npm @wasm-fmt/shfmt, a WASM build pinned exactly in devDependencies, so npm install supplies it everywhere and CI runs the same bytes — no hand-placed binary, unlike shellcheck. Run on write by the post-write core (scripts/lib/post-write.js) and on staged blobs by scripts/check-format-staged.js in .husky/pre-commit; ci.yml runs this in the lint job.
comments.scripts.check:sh:changed: check:sh over only the shell files that differ from HEAD, staged or unstaged, plus untracked new ones (#1015), picked by the same lister (#1828) — for an in-session check, since the full run has overrun a 300 s Bash call. Same flags and severity gate as check:sh, which owns their rationale. It waits on check:sh's shellcheck lock. It reads the worktree, so a neighbour's uncommitted shell edit is checked too. Its limit is -x's direction: sources are followed DOWNWARD only, so a changed scripts/lib/*.sh does not re-check the unchanged callers that source it — the full check:sh in CI does.
comments.scripts.check:py: ruff over every tracked .py file (mantahostels#1135). `ruff check .` from the repo root rather than a file list: ruff honours .gitignore, so it walks neither node_modules nor .next. The rule set lives in ruff.toml, which owns why it is what it is; do not restate it here. Installed from requirements-dev.txt (`ruff==0.16.4`) like the rest of the Python side, so `npm install` does NOT supply it and a fresh checkout has no ruff until `python3 -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt` runs — which is why the .husky/pre-commit half warns and PASSES when the binary is absent, exactly as the shellcheck and actionlint gates do. Unlike those two there IS a package-manager route, so the pin is real and scripts/test_requirements_pinned.py fails if the installed version and the pin disagree: bump the pin and reinstall in the same step. ci.yml runs this as a step in the EXISTING python job, which already does the pip install, so it costs no billed minute. `ruff format --check .` rides the same command since #1332, run on write by the post-write core (scripts/lib/post-write.js) and on staged blobs by scripts/check-format-staged.js in .husky/pre-commit.
comments.scripts.check:actions: actionlint over the 5 files in .github/workflows/ — the workflow YAML nothing else reads: Biome parses no YAML at all, and check:sh's file set is shell files, so the shell inside `run:` blocks reaches no other checker (mantahostels#1137). actionlint shells out to shellcheck for exactly those blocks, and additionally catches an undefined `needs:` job, an `if:` expression naming a context field that does not exist, and an unknown `runs-on:` label. Bare, with no path arguments and no flags: actionlint locates .github/workflows from the git root itself, which keeps the file set in one place rather than duplicating it here, and works in a worktree. THERE IS NO npm ROUTE — the npm package named `actionlint` is an unrelated third-party WASM wrapper (mantahostels#1137); do not install it. CI downloads the pinned linux_amd64 release tarball and checksums it (ci.yml's actionlint step); locally it is the same release's static aarch64 binary in ~/.local/bin, hand-placed as shellcheck's is (CLAUDE.md §Gotchas), so a fresh machine has neither. Run scoped, per staged path, by .husky/pre-commit since mantahostels#1137, which warns and PASSES when the binary is absent.
comments.scripts.prepare: husky writes core.hooksPath RELATIVE (.husky/_), and .husky/_ carries its own .gitignore of `*`, so a linked worktree resolved it to a directory that does not exist and ran no git hook at all (mantahostels#344). The re-pin must run inside `prepare`, because husky rewrites the value back to relative at every npm install. Use --git-common-dir, never $PWD: git config is repo-global, so an npm install run inside a worktree would otherwise point every tree's hooks at a directory that is about to be deleted. scripts/install-hooks.js does the re-pin, and points husky's shim at the committing tree's own .husky/<hook>, so a worktree runs and can test its own hook edits (#3138). Cost: the path is machine-specific, so moving or renaming the repo directory silently stops all hooks until the next npm install.
comments.allowScripts.unrs-resolver: Denied, not approved. unrs-resolver is the native module resolver ESLint reaches through eslint-config-next -> eslint-import-resolver-typescript; its postinstall runs napi-postinstall's checkAndPreparePackage, which fetches the platform binding when the optionalDependency route did not supply one. It did supply one here: @unrs/resolver-binding-linux-arm64-gnu is installed, and the resolver loads and resolves with no help from the script. So the script is a fallback for a case this machine is not in, and denying it costs nothing today. npm 11.16 treats the field as advisory (scripts still run; unreviewed ones are only listed), so this records the decision ahead of the release that enforces it. If a future install lands on a platform with no prebuilt binding, ESLint's import rules break loudly and the fix is to flip this to a pinned approval. Dev-scope only: no runtime path reaches it.
comments.devDependencies.js-yaml: Pinned exact, and to the version the tree already resolved through eslint -> @eslint/eslintrc, so the declaration dedupes onto the existing copy rather than installing a second. Declared rather than left transitive because scripts/check-workflow-permissions.js requires it by name (mantahostels#1209), as does scripts/check-skill-frontmatter.js (#887): if a future eslint drops that chain, an undeclared js-yaml turns both gates into a module-not-found at exit 2. The only YAML parser in the repo. Both consumers ship, and the plugin carries no node_modules, so each loads it from the host repo's own install through scripts/lib/host-package.js (#1380). No install script.
comments.devDependencies.@typescript-eslint/parse: Pinned exact, and to the version eslint-config-next already resolves, so the declaration dedupes onto the existing tree rather than installing a second copy. Declared rather than left transitive because eslint.config.mjs imports it by name (mantahostels#999): if a future eslint-config-next drops that chain, an undeclared parser makes `npm run lint` fail to load its own config.
comments.devDependencies.@next/eslint-plugin-next: Pinned exact, and to the version eslint-config-next already resolves, so the declaration dedupes onto the existing tree. Declared rather than left transitive because eslint.config.mjs imports it by name, which Biome's noUndeclaredDependencies refuses for an undeclared package (#1383). Bump it with eslint-config-next.
comments.devDependencies.eslint-plugin-react-hook: Pinned exact, and to the version eslint-config-next already resolves, so the declaration dedupes onto the existing tree. Declared rather than left transitive because eslint.config.mjs imports it by name and scripts/tooling-matrix.test.ts requires it, which Biome's noUndeclaredDependencies refuses for an undeclared package (#1383). Bump it with eslint-config-next.
comments.overrides.brace-expansion: Deliberately absent. GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (ReDoS) has no safe fix here: the advisory range <=5.0.7 swallows the whole 1.x line, and minimatch@3 still arrives via eslint-config-next's plugins (import, jsx-a11y, react) and eslint's own config-array/eslintrc. Forcing brace-expansion ^5 installs cleanly and lint passes, but it is a latent break, not a fix: v1 exported the function directly (module.exports = expand) while v5 exports a namespace ({ expand }), so minimatch@3's `require('brace-expansion')` yields an object and throws 'expand is not a function'. It only throws on patterns containing braces, because minimatch@3 short-circuits brace-free patterns (minimatch.js:266) — so it stays green until some plugin lints a {a,b} glob, then fails far from the cause. Dev-scope only: no runtime/production path reaches this. Revisit when eslint-config-next ships its plugins on minimatch 10.
comments.overrides.sharp: Deliberately absent (mantahostels#3559). next declares `sharp: ^0.35.3` as its own optionalDependency and is sharp's only dependent here, and an npm override REPLACES a spec rather than intersecting with it, so an entry below next's own spec silently LOWERS the floor instead of raising it. Check next's spec before re-adding one for the next libvips advisory.
comments.biome.--error-on-warnings: Four Biome invocations carry --error-on-warnings and must stay in step: scripts.check, scripts.check:staged, scripts.lint, and ci.yml's `Biome ci` step. Adopted at mantahostels#1445. WHY: a Biome run whose findings are all warnings exits 0, so a `recommended` rule whose default severity is warn is ON AND GATES NOTHING. The flag is a per-UPGRADE fix, not a per-rule one: the next Biome release adding a recommended rule at warn arrives gated instead of silent, and a rule whose heuristic does not fit this corpus is opted out with one "off" line in biome.json rather than opted in with one "error" line. INFO-SEVERITY RULES ARE NOT COVERED — the flag promotes warnings only — so each needs a name-by-name pin or a recorded decline (biome.json.linter.rules.info-severity-pins), and one a Biome upgrade adds arrives silent until it gets one. IT ADDS NO CONFIG-LEVEL RISK — a deprecated or unknown biome.json key already exits 1 either way, so mantahostels#1376's upgrade trap (a promoted nursery key is a hard config error, cleared by `biome migrate --write`) is unchanged. lint:fix and format deliberately do NOT carry it: both write rather than verdict, and --write already fixes what it can. DO NOT SOFTEN ONE SITE TO MATCH ANOTHER — pre-commit reads the commit's own staged paths (mantahostels#179) and catches the finding on the commit that introduces it; CI reads everything and is the only gate on drift arriving by a non-commit route, such as a Biome version bump.
comments.biome.json.linter.rules.nursery: Every nursery rule is pinned to "error" on purpose: nursery rules default to info or warn, and a Biome run whose only findings are infos or warnings exits 0, so an unpinned rule gates nothing (mantahostels#1063, mantahostels#1066). A rule here scoring zero findings is a clean corpus, not a dead rule (mantahostels#1376) — never prune one for never firing. Rules for frameworks this repo does not use (Playwright, Vue, Svelte, Qwik, React Native, Drizzle) were declined: the session that adds a framework turns on that framework's rules against the Biome shipping then. noUnnecessaryTemplateExpression (literals split on purpose), useDomQuerySelector, useRegexpExec, useNamedCaptureGroup and useUnicodeRegex stay off on merit grounds (#1318 round 1). UPGRADING BIOME: run `biome migrate --write` first. A bump that promotes a pinned rule out of nursery leaves a key Biome refuses outright, and Biome then lints NOTHING — in .husky/pre-commit and in CI alike — until the key moves. migrate relocates a promoted key automatically with its severity preserved; a rule removed rather than promoted is a hand-delete, and migrate stays silent on that one. noUntrustedLicenses reads the license field of each package named in THIS package.json only — a transitive dependency is invisible to it (mantahostels#1398). Its policy (#1318 Q3 (C), #1353 Q1 (A)): no source-available and no GNU-family copyleft direct dependency, in the closed-source product or in the plugin shipped to other repos; file-level copyleft (MPL, EPL, CDDL) is allowed. So requireOsiApproved is on, and deny lists every GPL, LGPL and AGPL SPDX id, -only and -or-later; the deprecated bare spellings (GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0+) already fail its default of "present, valid, non-deprecated SPDX identifier", ignoreDeprecated staying false. It reports on package.json, so the staged-path pre-commit gate raises it only on a commit that stages package.json — the commit that adds a dependency — and it passes silently in a worktree, which has no node_modules.
comments.biome.json.files.includes: `!.local` is excluded because `.local/` is untracked scratch that is NOT gitignored, so `useIgnoreFile` never reaches it, and sessions put throwaway git WORKTREES there. Each worktree carries its own `biome.json`, which Biome reads as a nested root configuration and REFUSES on at config discovery — repo-wide, so it fires even when Biome is handed explicit paths, and every pre-commit gate in the shared tree fails while one exists. A `files.includes` exclusion does suppress that discovery: a nested config under the already-excluded `.claude/tmp/` is invisible to Biome. Bare `!.local` and not `!.local/**`, matching the sibling directory entries. Vitest has the same hole and its own fix (`vitest.config.ts`'s `exclude`); neither substitutes for the other (mantahostels#2206). `!.claude/skills/*/.claude-plugin/types` is a mod's copy of the engine's own type declarations (760 KB, written by Claude Code, not this repo), which the mod type-checks against and nobody edits (#854).
comments.biome.json.overrides.engine-modules: noUndeclaredDependencies is off under `.claude/skills/wfc-*/**` and `hooks/**` (#1383): the plugin's entry module `hooks/register.ts` and each mod's hooks, tests and types import `claude-code` or `claude-code/testing`, which the Claude Code engine supplies at load time and no package.json can declare. The rule's options choose which package.json sections count and cannot exempt one module by name, so the exemption is by path.
comments.biome.json.linter.rules.style.useNamingC: Base §G5's scheme, repo-wide at error with no override, tests included, configured as #1418 specifies (#1328 Q1 (A), Q2 (A)). `objectLiteralMember` and `typeMember` take `match: ".*"` because Biome cannot tell a house key from an external one (env-var names, hook payload keys, GitHub API keys); listing all four formats still fires on `_schema`, `$note` and the like. `strictCase: false` because §G5 sets no acronym casing, so `readJSON` and `toolUseID` pass. What stays with review is in docs/code-standards.md §W.
comments.biome.json.overrides.cognitive-complexit: noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity refuses over 15, Biome's default, in app/, lib/, scripts/ and .claude/ (mantahostels#1518; widened at #1400). #1318 Q2 (A) put scripts/ and .claude/ under it on merit: the session guards, pickers and arbiter there run in every session, so a tangled function in them is the one whose change breaks every session at once. Its own override, not top level, because the ruling names those four paths only. Never narrow it back on the old burndown-cost ground.
comments.biome.json.overrides.mod-tests: `noDoneCallback` is off for every mod's tests, `.claude/skills/wfc-*/tests/` (#854, #865): the `claude plugin test` kit hands every test body `($, on)`, and the rule reads that second parameter as a done-callback.
comments.biome.json.linter.rules.info-severity-pi: Rules across complexity, correctness and style are pinned to "error" on purpose (mantahostels#1447, #1381). WHY: they are `recommended` rules whose DEFAULT SEVERITY IS INFO, and --error-on-warnings promotes warnings only — an info-only run exits 0 with the flag on — so they were on, reported and gating nothing. All score ZERO findings on this corpus; that is a clean corpus, not a dead rule, so never prune one for never firing. The seventeen dead-code complexity rules (noExtraBooleanCast, noFlatMapIdentity and the fifteen noUseless*) flag code that is provably dead or a provable no-op, which this repo already treats as a defect class: mantahostels#1444 pinned tsc's allowUnreachableCode and allowUnusedLabels flat at zero on the same ground. useParseIntRadix is a defect rule outright (omitting the radix changes what the string parses to). useNodejsImportProtocol rests on the client bundle, NOT on shadowing — Node resolves core modules ahead of node_modules, so an npm package named `fs` cannot shadow the builtin; the risk is a bare `fs` reachable from a 'use client' file getting a silent empty browser stub where `node:fs` fails loudly. useLiteralKeys stays unpinned (on at info, gating nothing), clashing with noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature (#1316). DECLINED at mantahostels#1447, do not add them: noDuplicateFields — GraphQL only, and a framework's rules are turned on by the commit that adds it; useArrayLiterals — measured to MISS its own defect class, since it ignores `new Array(n)`, the hole-creating form, and fires only on `new Array()` and `new Array(a, b)`.
comments.biome.json.linter.rules.repo-wide: #1318 ruled 32 Biome rules on at "error" repo-wide, on merit. DEFECT RULES (#1318 Q4 (A)) refuse code that is wrong wherever it sits: a rethrow dropping its cause, a shadowed name, an empty block with no reason, an element id that collides when its component renders twice, an undeclared import. SPELLING RULES (#1318 Q1 (A)): one tool-enforced spelling is a merit where it reads at least as clearly as the alternative and raises no false findings, so an agent copies one form from the code around it. Never switch either group off on the old corpus-size or fix-up-cost grounds; re-judge a rule on merit only. docs/code-standards.md §W lists them.
